items.prompt: When is this sample excess-return ratio undefined?

options.why: A negative return can be valid.

options.text: Whenever mean excess return is zero, even with positive sample standard deviation
options.why: Zero divided by a positive standard deviation is a defined ratio of zero.

options.text: Only when both excess-return mean and standard deviation equal zero
options.why: A zero standard deviation makes the ratio undefined regardless of its numerator.

options.text: When sample excess-return standard deviation is 0
options.why: Division by zero does not establish infinite skill.

items.explanation: An explicit no-result state is safer than inventing an impressive ratio.
